results.title: The Afternoon house
results.brief_description: An experimental film showing the fascination of an old house and its garden for a small girl. She goes there to retrieve a lost ball, and wanders about looking at the trees and flowers first, and then going through the Georgian doorway and up the staircase exploring the rooms, looking at the pictures, trying an old fashioned cane chair and then, becoming engrossed in her surroundings, she knocks over a vase of daisies and is frightened as she sees ugly masks staring at her from the walls. She dashes downstairs and out the gate without stopping even to retrieve her ball. Photographed by Mike Browning, music by Allan Lee.

results.title: The Action of the clinical thermometer
results.brief_description: This film shows the non-continuous movement of mercury past the restriction in the glass tube of a clinical thermometer. An example of the use of cinematography in scientific research, this film is the first case in which cinematography through a microscope has been combined with high-speed cinematography at 3000 frames per second.

results.title: The Accursed architect
results.creator_credit: Pierre Cast and La Societe Nouvelle Pathe-Cinema
results.brief_description: An investigation of the work and theories of Claude-Nicolas Ledoux, 1736-1806, an architect and innovator two centuries before his time. Initially he created chateaux for the French nobility, but later he became an urbanist, designing houses and cities for the working man. However, his utopian dream that architecture should be related to daily life was not realised.

results.title: Thamesmead '68
results.brief_description: Thamesmead is a new community being developed on the site of the Royal Arsenal by the London Borough Councils of Greenwich and Bexley, co-operating with government departments, private developers and representatives of many organisations. Its 17,000 homes will provide a new community for 60,000 Londoners. Shows the thinking and planning that has gone into Thamesmead.

results.brief_description: Demonstrates the significance of texture in painting and in everyday life. Painters Phoebe Flory and Eliot O’Hara explain the thinking behind the use of textures, with illustrative examples that span the history of art from the Ming Dynasty to today’s non-objective painters.
